Tousled

TOW-zuld · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Tousled is having hair or an appearance made messily but lightly disordered, in a casual, ruffled, or windswept way.

The photographer actually preferred the model's tousled, just-out-of-bed look to anything a stylist could arrange.

Worked Example

After the puppy dragged the blanket across the whole living room, it ended up in a tousled heap by the door.

The blanket wasn't torn or dirty -- it was just dragged into a messy, disordered pile, which is exactly what tousled describes.

How Tousled Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

rumpled

rumpled: messily disordered, as if pulled about

disheveled

disheveled: untidy, especially in hair or clothing

Antonyms

sleek

sleek: smooth and neat in appearance

groomed

groomed: carefully tidied and cared for

How Strong Is It? — mussed → tousled → matted

mussed vs. tousled

mussed vs. tousled: Mussed hair is only slightly out of place, a much milder disorder than fully tousled hair.

matted vs. tousled

matted vs. tousled: Matted hair is tangled into thick, stuck-together clumps, an even messier state than simply tousled.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — touse / tussle

root — touse / tussle: to handle roughly, to pull or drag about (Middle English, Germanic origin)

suffix — -le / -led

suffix — -le / -led: forms a verb or adjective describing a repeated action (English)

Put it together

Put it together: Tousled comes from the same old root as tussle -- both trace back to a Middle English word meaning 'to handle roughly, to pull about.' Hair that's been tousled looks like it has been playfully pulled and rumpled.

Use the root in a new word: tussle

Use the root in a new word: tussle: The two puppies had a friendly tussle over the rope toy before flopping down to nap.

Word Choice

Tousled is often used warmly, even affectionately -- tousled hair can look playful or charming, unlike unkempt, which usually suggests neglect rather than a casual, windblown look.
